title: ChatGPT yeni Intelligent UI arayüzü ve GPT-6 ile görselleşiyor
summary: OpenAI, ChatGPT için sohbetleri etkileşimli grafikler, hesap makineleri ve özel araçlarla zenginleştiren Intelligent UI özelliğini duyurdu.
body:
ChatGPT yeni Intelligent UI arayüzü ile birlikte gelen GPT-6 modeli sayesinde artık metin odaklı yapısını geride bırakarak çok daha görsel ve etkileşimli bir deneyim sunmaya hazırlanıyor. TechCrunch ve WIRED sitelerinin aktardığına göre, kullanıcılar bundan böyle sadece düz metinler yerine tıklanabilir butonlar, özel hesap makineleri ve düzenlenebilir grafiklerle karşılaşacak. 

## Akıllı arayüz neler sunuyor?

OpenAI'ın açıklamalarına göre yeni özellik, karmaşık konuların öğrenilmesini kolaylaştırmayı hedefliyor. Kullanıcılar bir uçak kanadının nasıl çalıştığını, bisiklet mekanizmalarını veya tarifleri görsel şemalarla keşfedebilecek. **Intelligent UI**, kullanıcıların taleplerine göre özel araçlar da üretebiliyor; örneğin seyahat planları, kişisel tasarruf hesaplayıcıları ve interaktif haritalar bu yenilikler arasında yer alıyor. Görsellerin yoğunluğunu istemeyen kullanıcılar ise bu ayarı diledikleri gibi azaltabilecek.

## Erişim ve dağıtım takvimi

Sisteme güç veren GPT-6 modeli, Pro, Plus, Business ve Enterprise aboneleri için kullanıma sunulurken, ücretsiz ve alt kademedeki kullanıcılar bu yeniliğe sonraki gün erişebilecek. Yapılan gösterimlerde, sistemin sadece bilgi vermekle kalmayıp aynı zamanda kullanıcıların veriler üzerinde doğrudan değişiklik yapmasına olanak tanıdığı da gösterildi.

**Neden önemli?** Sohbet botlarının metin duvarları ötesine geçerek etkileşimli arayüzler üretmesi, yapay zekanın yazılım dünyasındaki rolünü kökten değiştiriyor.

source_texts.title: ChatGPT is getting a lot more visual, with the launch of a new interface
source_texts.summary: OpenAI is launching a new user interface that will bring interactive visuals to ChatGPT.
source_texts.text:
ChatGPT is about to get a lot more visual, thanks to a new feature that OpenAI calls Intelligent UI. The new interface, which is being rolled out Wednesday with a new GPT-6 model, will integrate a significant amount of visuals into users’ conversations.
OpenAI says many of those visuals will be interactive. In other words, instead of just flat, cartoonish pictures, the chatbot will frequently include things like tappable buttons, a customized calculator for a specific task, interactive charts, editable graphs, and other elements the user can work with directly.
The big goal here, according to OpenAI is to make “learning complex topics easier.” It may also make ChatGPT friendlier and more accessible and help bring in a wider audience, though OpenAI didn’t say so directly.
In a call with journalists, OpenAI staff gave a brief demonstration of Intelligent UI’s capabilities, showing how the new chatbot can instantly whip up various diagrams and visuals that help users understand more abstract topics.
Aarush Selvan, a product manager at the company, said that while “ChatGPT has predominantly been a text-based interface,” the company really wants to help users “get things done — from everyday things like planning a recipe or a trip or even trying to learn something, adding that the most helpful answers aren’t just text.”
Selvan gave the example of a college student wanting to know how an airplane wing functions. He asked ChatGPT to “explore how an airplane wing generates lift” and the chatbot quickly spun up a number of diagrams designed to show how planes stay in the air.
Other examples from the company included things like visuals for recipes, a diagram explaining bicycle mechanics, a map for a multi-day hiking excursion, a personal savings calculator, and more.
This new feature will be customizable. As with other aspects of ChatGPT’s personality, if users don’t want so many visuals in their responses, they’ll be able to dial them back. Intelligent UI rolls out globally with GPT-6 for Pro, Plus, Business, and Enterprise users, and arrives Thursday for users of the free and lower-cost Go tiers.

source_texts.title: The New ChatGPT Is More Show Than Tell
source_texts.summary: OpenAI is updating ChatGPT for all users with an “Intelligent UI” that’s more visual—generating interactive elements as part of the chatbot’s outputs.
source_texts.text:
When you ask a chatbot a question, you’ll often get a wall of text back, maybe with an image or two pulled from the web. That may no longer be the case soon as OpenAI overhauls how ChatGPT answers prompts.
On Wednesday, OpenAI unveiled an “Intelligent UI” update for ChatGPT that generates visual, custom elements—when helpful—for answering a user's questions. The company's new experience is powered by its recent GPT-6 model, which rolls out to paid users today and free users tomorrow.
I got a quick test of the user interface before launch, and these visual elements felt like a welcome change. When I asked for a diagram of a slug, ChatGPT generated an anatomy-focused visual with buttons I could press for each different part, from the upper tentacles to the muscular foot. I also generated a San Francisco apartment affordability calculator with movable sliders to adjust income and other expenses, showing what percentage of my take-home pay different units would cost.
My favorite part of this quick hands-on with ChatGPT’s Intelligent UI was an airplane seat explorer. I’m not a fan of sitting in the exit rows, so I asked ChatGPT to generate a custom tool to compare the cabin layouts between four different Alaska and Delta planes. In its output, I could tap any seat on the map for more details, and ChatGPT highlighted the exit rows in green.
While useful in some results, every ChatGPT answer won’t suddenly include a chart or graphic. “We have a design team that spent a lot of time figuring out when adding a diagram, chart, or buttons adds value versus when it's starting to feel cluttered,” says Aarush Selvan, a product manager at OpenAI. If a user isn’t interested in visuals, they can tell ChatGPT to generate fewer of those outputs.
These visual results are similar to what Google announced earlier this year for Search when it expanded the bespoke results users may see. Google’s version is called “generative UI.” One example: if you want to understand deep space better, Search can output an adjustable graphic that breaks down how black holes work using multiple sliders.
Chatbot experiences have increasingly become multimodal, meaning that text, images, and voice blend into one user experience. OpenAI's launch of an updated ChatGPT that's easier on the eyes and more interactive for over a billion users signals that the multimodal era is here. However, a larger shift toward generative user interfaces may spark an identity crisis for designers, as AI dictates more of what software looks like for individual users.
With AI tools now able to quickly generate custom software, the future of chatbots is further personalized and attuned to what I want to see, and what I want to see is slug diagrams. Good riddance to walls of text.
